deep.reconstruction:
Context: the surrounding folios belong to Riemann's work on the approximate functional equation, the material Siegel (1932) edited as the Riemann–Siegel formula. The next page computes Gaussian/Fresnel integrals and parabolic-cylinder-type ODEs. The key structural signal here is the derivative order 3n-4m. The Riemann–Siegel correction terms have exactly this form, C_n = sum_m d_{n,m} Phi^{(3n-4m)}(p); for example C_1 involves Phi''' and C_2 involves Phi^{(6)} and Phi''. This page appears to derive a recursion for the numerical coefficients of that expansion.

(0) Preliminary recursions (top two lines). The first line is struck out: a_n = (alpha/(pi i)) a_{n+1} + (3n+2)(3n+4) a_{n+3}/(16(pi i)^2). The second line is a_{3n-4} = a_{3n-1}(3n-1)(3n-2)/(16 pi i). My reading of the second: it is the ascending-power-series recursion for the Airy-type equation (1/(16 pi i)) v'' = z v. Put v = sum a_k z^k and compare z^{k-2}. This gives a_{k-3} = a_k k(k-1)/(16 pi i), and k = 3n-1 reproduces the written line. Equivalently it is the z*alpha term alone with alpha = 1.

(1) The ODE. Riemann writes (1/(8 pi i)) v'' - v(2 pi i z^2 + 2 z alpha) = 0. Halved, this is
  (1/(16 pi i)) v'' - pi i z^2 v - alpha z v = 0.
He seeks a formal solution in descending powers of z and in powers of 1/alpha:
  v = sum a_n^m z^{-3n-1+4m} alpha^{-n}, with 3n >= 4m.
Then v'' = sum a_n^m (3n+1-4m)(3n+2-4m) z^{-3n-3+4m} alpha^{-n}.
Collect the coefficient of z^{-3n+4m}. It receives three contributions:
- v'' at index (n-1, m), carrying alpha^{-n+1};
- z^2 v at index (n-1, m-1), carrying alpha^{-n+1};
- z v at index (n, m), carrying alpha^{-n}.
The factor alpha in alpha z v equalizes the powers of alpha. The result is the recursion written on the page:
  a_{n-1}^m (3n-2-4m)(3n-1-4m)/(16 pi i) - pi i a_{n-1}^{m-1} - a_n^m = 0, for 3n > 4m.
With a_0^0 = 1 (leading term 1/z) this gives a_1^0 = 1/(8 pi i), a_2^0 = 5/(32 (pi i)^2), a_2^1 = -1/8, and so on.

(2) A side remark on zeta. Riemann writes Pi(s-1) zeta(s) = Pi(s-1) sum_{n=1}^m n^{-s} + int_0^oo e^{-mx}/(e^x - 1) x^{s-1} dx, with s = 1/2 + ti. This follows from Gamma(s) n^{-s} = int_0^oo e^{-nx} x^{s-1} dx summed over n > m, since sum_{n>m} e^{-nx} = e^{-mx}/(e^x - 1). It is the starting point for splitting off the partial sum of the approximate functional equation.

(3) Transfer to derivatives. Insert the Taylor series f(s+z) = sum f^{(nu)}(s) z^nu / nu! and integrate around z = 0. Only nu = 3n-4m contributes to the residue. After a scaling that introduces t (implicitly z -> tz; my interpretation), this gives
  u(s,t) = oint v f(s+z) dz = 2 pi i sum a_n^m alpha^{-n} f^{(3n-4m)}(s) t^{3n-4m}/(3n-4m)!.
This is precisely the Riemann–Siegel shape: a combination of the derivatives f^{(3n-4m)}.

(4) A PDE for u, by bookkeeping. Riemann lists the three monomials a_{n-1}^m f^{(3n+3-4m)} alpha^{-n+1}, a_{n-1}^{m-1} f^{(3n+1-4m)} and a_n^m f^{(3n-4m)}. He then computes:
- t^2 d^4u/ds^4, whose (n-1, m) term becomes a_{n-1}^m alpha^{-n+1} (3n-2-4m)(3n-1-4m) f^{(3n+1-4m)} t^{3n-1-4m}/(3n-1-4m)!;
- d^2u/dt^2, whose (n-1, m-1) term becomes a_{n-1}^{m-1} alpha^{-n+1} f^{(3n+1-4m)} t^{3n-1-4m}/(3n-1-4m)!;
- d^2u/(ds dt), whose (n, m) term becomes a_n^m alpha^{-n} f^{(3n+1-4m)} t^{3n-1-4m}/(3n-1-4m)!.
The recursion then translates into the PDE
  (1/(16 pi i)) t^2 u_ssss - pi i u_tt - c u_st = 0.
The page as transcribed has c = 1/alpha. Consistency with (1) requires c = alpha; see errors.

Purpose: to generate systematically the coefficients d_{n,m} of the Riemann–Siegel correction terms (derivatives of order 3n-4m of the basic kernel), via a three-term recursion, and to package them as a linear PDE.
errors: The final PDE as transcribed has -(1/alpha) d^2u/(ds dt). With v = sum a_n^m z^{-3n-1+4m} alpha^{-n} and the recursion written above it, the a_{n-1} terms carry alpha^{-n+1} while the a_n^m term carries alpha^{-n}. The mixed term must therefore be -alpha d^2u/(ds dt), or else the first two terms must be divided by alpha. Either Riemann slipped or the transcription misreads the factor.

The integral formula Pi(s-1) zeta(s) = Pi(s-1) sum_1^m n^{-s} + int_0^oo e^{-mx} x^{s-1}/(e^x-1) dx holds only for Re s > 1. At s = 1/2 + ti the integral diverges at x = 0, since the integrand behaves like x^{s-2}. Riemann does not state the analytic continuation (e.g. a Hankel-type loop contour) needed on the critical line.
The factor t^{3n-4m} in u is not explained on the page. It presumably comes from replacing f(s+z) by f(s+tz); this is my interpretation.
The first line, a crossed-out recursion with (3n+2)(3n+4)/(16(pi i)^2), is inconsistent with the later normalisation and was rightly discarded.

results.what: Formal series solution v = sum a_n^m z^{-3n-1+4m} alpha^{-n} of (1/(16 pi i)) v'' = (pi i z^2 + alpha z) v, with the three-term recursion a_n^m = a_{n-1}^m (3n-2-4m)(3n-1-4m)/(16 pi i) - pi i a_{n-1}^{m-1}
results.modern_name: Recursion for the coefficients d_{n,m} of the Riemann–Siegel asymptotic correction terms C_n = sum d_{n,m} Phi^{(3n-4m)}
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's Nachlass as edited by C.L. Siegel (1932); the recursion was later systematised by Gabcke (1979)

results.what: Pi(s-1)zeta(s) = Pi(s-1) sum_{n<=m} n^{-s} + int_0^oo e^{-mx} x^{s-1}/(e^x-1) dx
results.modern_name: Mellin representation of the Hurwitz zeta tail Gamma(s) zeta(s, m+1)

results.what: Residue extraction: oint v(z) f(s+tz) dz = 2 pi i sum a_n^m alpha^{-n} f^{(3n-4m)}(s) t^{3n-4m}/(3n-4m)!, plus a fourth-order PDE satisfied by u
results.modern_name: Operator / generating-function form of the Riemann–Siegel coefficient expansion

results.what: Ascending series recursion a_{k-3} = a_k k(k-1)/(16 pi i) for v'' = 16 pi i z v
results.modern_name: Power-series solution of the Airy equation

deep.surprise_reason: This is part of the Riemann–Siegel material that Siegel published from these very papers in 1932; the 3n-4m derivative structure and a recursion for the coefficients are known to be Riemann's. The explicit PDE packaging is a notable working detail but not a new attribution.

checkable.asserts: Truncated v satisfies the ODE (1/(16 pi i)) v'' - pi i z^2 v - alpha z v = 0: the coefficients of R vanish for all monomials alpha^{-n} with n<=3, the residual being truncation terms only.
The recursion gives a_1^0 = 1/(8 pi i) from a_0^0 = 1; the result is 0.
The second derivative of z^{-3n-1+4m} has coefficient (3n+1-4m)(3n+2-4m); the result is 0.
Placeholder; the real check: substituting v=sum a_k z^k into v''/(16 pi i) - z v gives a_{k-3} = a_k k(k-1)/(16 pi i), which matches a_{3n-4} = a_{3n-1}(3n-1)(3n-2)/(16 pi i) at k=3n-1.

checkable.sympy: x=symbols('x',positive=True); s=3; mm=2; N(gamma(s)*zeta(s) - gamma(s)*sum(Rational(1,j**s) for j in range(1,mm+1)) - Integral(exp(-mm*x)*x**(s-1)/(exp(x)-1),(x,0,oo)))
checkable.asserts: Gamma(s)zeta(s) = Gamma(s) sum_{n<=m} n^{-s} + int_0^oo e^{-mx} x^{s-1}/(e^x-1) dx for s=3, m=2; the result is numerically 0.

# compare coefficient structure of t**2*diff(u,s,4)/(16*pi*I) - pi*I*diff(u,t,2) - al*diff(u,s,t)
checkable.asserts: Using the recursion, (1/(16 pi i)) t^2 u_ssss - pi i u_tt - alpha u_st = 0 holds termwise. It requires the factor alpha (not 1/alpha) on the mixed derivative.

transcription_corrections: In the expanded-sum line, the terms '[-...-] pi sum a_n^m z^{-3n+1+4m}' should read '- pi i sum a_n^{m} z^{-3n+1+4m} alpha^{-n}', i.e. the pi i z^2 v contribution, consistent with the recursion.
The ODE '1/(8 pi i) d^2v/dz^2 - v(2 pi i zz + 2 z alpha) =' is followed by an empty right-hand side, to be read as '= 0'. It is equivalent to the 1/(16 pi i) form used afterwards.
In the u formula, f^{3n-4m}(s) and f^{3n+1-4m} denote derivatives f^{(3n-4m)}(s) etc., not powers.
In the final PDE, the coefficient of d^2u/(ds dt) is transcribed as 1/alpha. On mathematical grounds it should be alpha; the image is ambiguous ('- 1 d^2u / alpha ds dt' may be a misreading).
